hook.line: Hernando's bus is always the subject of a complaint, but "it was late" and "it took ages" are two different complaints in Spanish. Pick the wrong one and you have blamed the wrong thing.
hook.es: El bus se demoró una hora.

examples.es: El bus se demoró una hora.
Me demoré mucho en encontrar la casa.
examples.en: It took me ages to find the house.

examples.es: ¿Cuánto te demoras en llegar al trabajo?
examples.en: How long does it take you to get to work? (to a friend)
Vale got to the café late.
It takes me twenty minutes to get there.

rule:
English says *late* for two different things. Spanish splits them.

*How long it takes*: *demorarse* (everyday in Colombia) or *tardar*, followed by *en* and the action. *Me demoro veinte minutos en llegar.* *Tardo veinte minutos en llegar.*

*Arriving after the agreed time*: *llegar tarde*. *Llegué tarde.* The opposite is *llegar a tiempo*.

So *El bus se demoró una hora* says the trip was slow. *El bus llegó tarde* says it missed the schedule. A bus can take an hour and still arrive on time.
smallPrint: Teachers call this duration versus lateness: *tardar* and *demorarse* measure time, *llegar tarde* measures against a schedule.

readAndPick.es: El bus se demoró una hora.
options: The bus took an hour.
The bus was an hour late.
The bus left an hour ago.
The bus took long.
The bus was late.
The bus is coming.
The meeting took long.
I took a long time to arrive.
I was late to the meeting.

readAndPick.es: Me demoré mucho en encontrar la casa.
options: It took me ages to find the house.
I was late finding the house.
I found the house too early.
I am twenty minutes late.
It takes me twenty minutes to get there.
I arrived twenty minutes ago.
Vale is always late.
Vale always takes long.
Vale always arrives on time.

readAndPick.es: ¿Cuánto te demoras en llegar al trabajo?
options: How late are you getting to work?
How long does it take you to get to work?
When do you get to work?

readAndPick.es: Llegamos tarde porque el tráfico se demoró.
options: We arrived late because traffic is slow.
We took long because we were late.
We were late because the traffic took a long time.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (The bus took an hour): El bus ___ una hora. (se demoró / llegó tarde)
yourTurn.answer: El bus se demoró una hora.
yourTurn.why: You are saying how long it took, so *se demoró*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose the right form and type the whole sentence (The bus was late): El bus ___. (se demoró / llegó tarde)
yourTurn.why: Missing the agreed time is *llegó tarde*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (I): It took me ages to find the house.
yourTurn.answer: Me demoré mucho en encontrar la casa.
accept: Tardé mucho en encontrar la casa.
yourTurn.why: Duration uses *demorarse* or *tardar*, then *en* and the verb.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (to a friend): How long does it take you to get to work?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Cuánto te demoras en llegar al trabajo?
yourTurn.why: *Cuánto* asks about time taken, and *te demoras* is for a friend.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (I): I was late to the meeting.
yourTurn.why: Being late for something agreed is *llegué tarde*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about duration: Vale llegó tarde al café. (it took Vale an hour to get to the café)
yourTurn.answer: Vale se demoró una hora en llegar al café.
accept: Vale tardó una hora en llegar al café.
yourTurn.why: Now you measure time taken, so *se demoró* and *en llegar*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish (I, in general): I always arrive on time.
yourTurn.why: The opposite of *llegar tarde* is *llegar a tiempo*.

pitfalls.right: Me demoré una hora en llegar al café.
pitfalls.why: Almost. To say how long something took, use *demorarse* or *tardar* plus *en*.
Being late for something is *llegar tarde*; *demorarse* only measures time.
After *tardar* the little word is *en*, not *a*.
Almost. Late is something you do on arrival, so use *llegar tarde*.

personal: Tell us how long it takes you to get to your work or school, and whether you usually arrive on time. Use *me demoro* or *tardo*, and *llego a tiempo* or *llego tarde*.
